title: Holidays in Two Countries
text:
Holidays are special days. In Japan, people celebrate a holiday called Obon in summer. Families visit their old homes and cook special food together. The children often dance in the street.

In Mexico, people celebrate Independence Day in September. There are parades, music and red, white and green flags. Many people wear bright clothes. Families eat together at night.

questions.text: When do people in Japan celebrate Obon?
What colors are the flags in Mexico's celebration?
Why do you think families cook special food together?
options: They want to spend time together

questions.text: What is the main idea of this passage?
options: Holidays are celebrated in different ways

paragraph_translations: Las festividades son días especiales. En Japón, la gente celebra una festividad llamada Obon en verano. Las familias visitan sus antiguas casas y cocinan comida especial juntas. Los niños a menudo bailan en la calle.

En México, la gente celebra el Día de la Independencia en septiembre. Hay desfiles, música y banderas rojas, blancas y verdes. Muchas personas usan ropa de colores brillantes. Las familias comen juntas por la noche.
